text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12.54px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica Neue', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #f0efec

g.text: Physicians who got more in their first year rose more, but they were different physicians

text.style: font-size: 9.69px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica Neue', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #c3c2b7

g.text: Change in the probability of ≥ 11 claims of the paid brand, percentage points, average of years 0–3 after the first payment

text.style: font-size: 7.41px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica Neue', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Groups by promotional dollars and contacts for the brand in the year of the first payment; bars: 95% CIs clustered by practice. 92%–97% of newly paid physicians got under $100 that year

text.style: font-size: 7.41px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica Neue', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: (mostly sponsored meals). Bigger first-year payments go to physicians who differ in ways matching cannot fully capture, so this gradient is descriptive, not a dose-response.

text.style: font-size: 7.41px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica Neue', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Associations, not proof that payments changed prescribing.

text.style: font-size: 7.41px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica Neue', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Source: CMS Open Payments (general payments, promotional natures); CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers.
